title: Pickup at 3:15
premise: A divorced mom discovers her ex's new girlfriend has been secretly picking up their daughter from school — and assumes she's being edged out, until she learns her daughter arranged it to hide something.
synopsis: A new school text alert tells ER nurse Dana that her ex-husband's girlfriend signed their daughter out on Dana's day. Marcus is evasive, Renée is apologetic but vague, and Dana's lawyer friend sees a custody play taking shape. But the messages on her daughter's iPad tell a different story — one a nine-year-old has been carrying alone.

characters.name: Dana Whitfield
characters.description: ER nurse on 12-hour shifts. Fiercely protective, tired, quick to read threats. Efficient and punctuation-correct; 'K.' when angry.

characters.name: Marcus Bell
characters.description: Runs an HVAC business. Loves Lily; avoids conflict by under-informing. Short replies, 👍.

characters.name: Renée Okafor
characters.description: Middle-school art teacher; together with Marcus eight months. Careful, warm, apologetic; complete sentences.

characters.name: Lily Bell
characters.description: Third grader with a kid iPad on Dana's Apple ID. Bright, private, loves drawing and basketball. Emoji strings, 'ya', spelling slips, never answers directly.

characters.name: Tasha Grant
characters.description: Strategic, wants receipts. Brisk, numbered lists, 'screenshot that'.

characters.name: Jenna Alvarez
characters.description: Mom of Lily's classmate Maya. Friendly, careful.

relationships.description: Divorced two years; civil but brittle. Dana has Lily Mon–Thu, Marcus Fri–Sun.
Lily trusts Renée because she 'doesn't make a big deal'.

centralConflict: Dana's fear of losing her place in Lily's life against Marcus's and Renée's secrecy — and, underneath, a child handling bullying alone because she sees her parents as already at war.

secrets.description: Lily asked Renée to drive her from school to the Y on Thursdays (Feb 19, Feb 26, Mar 5, Mar 12) instead of riding the Y bus, telling her 'mom knows'.
Marcus knew Renée was 'helping out' on Thursdays and assumed Dana had agreed.
Two fifth graders on the Thursday Y bus took Lily's water bottle and sketchbook and mocked her ('here, Bell Bell').
Lily told no parent because 'you guys would fight'.

plannedEnding: Bittersweet: the school removes the fifth graders from the Y bus and adds a monitor, and Lily gets her sketchbook back, but her reason for silence — 'you guys would fight' — lands hard. Dana deletes the lawyer's draft and she, Marcus, Renée and Lily start a shared pickup group chat that Lily renames 'team chat 🏀'.
continuity: Custody: Dana has Lily Mon–Thu; Marcus Fri–Sun. Handover Friday after school, return Sunday 6 PM.
On Thursdays Dana works 7:00 AM–7:30 PM; Lily normally rides the after-school bus to the YMCA program and Dana collects her at 7:30.
Renée was added to the school pickup list by Marcus in January 'for emergencies'. She drove Lily to the Y on Feb 19, Feb 26, Mar 5 and Mar 12.
The school's text pickup alerts started on Mar 5, 2026.
Lily's iPad is signed into Dana's Apple ID, so its messages sync to Dana's phone.
Lily's classmate Maya (Jenna's daughter) knew about the bullying and was sworn to secrecy.
Resolution: Mr. Patel rides the Thursday Y bus; the two fifth graders were moved off it; the sketchbook was found in the fifth-grade lost and found.
New group chat (Dana, Marcus, Renée, Lily) named 'team chat 🏀' by Lily; all pickup changes go there first.

timeline.event: Marcus adds Renée to the school pickup list.
Lily first asks Renée to pick her up, claiming her mom knows.
First school SMS alert reaches Dana.
Office confirms three pickups; Marcus says he'll handle it.
Handover argument; Tasha drafts an email.
Renée, Jenna and Lily fill in the truth.
Dana and Marcus meet the school together.

unresolvedThreads.description: Why is Renée picking Lily up on Dana's days?
Is Marcus building a custody case?
Can Dana and Marcus stop fighting long enough to help Lily?

partSummaries.title: Authorized Adult
partSummaries.summary: Mid-shift, Dana gets the school's new pickup alert: Renée signed Lily out. Marcus is evasive, Renée politely refuses to explain, and Lily changes the subject. Tasha tells her to find out how many times — the answer is three Thursdays. Marcus promises to handle it. A week later, another alert arrives while Dana is on shift.

partSummaries.title: I Thought You Knew
partSummaries.summary: Marcus admits Renée told him she was 'helping out' on Thursdays and he assumed Dana knew. Tasha drafts a firm email and names Dana's real fear: a paper trail that makes her shifts look like a problem. Then Renée's reply arrives on Dana's phone calling her 'sweetie' — Lily's iPad is synced to Dana's account, and the thread shows Lily begging Renée not to tell.

partSummaries.title: Thursdays
partSummaries.summary: Renée owns her mistake but won't break Lily's trust over text — she tells Dana to ask why Thursdays. Jenna, a classmate's mom, reveals two fifth graders on the Thursday Y bus have been taking Lily's things and mocking her. Lily, texting from her bedroom so she doesn't have to look at her mom, admits it — and explains why she told no one.

partSummaries.title: Team Chat
partSummaries.summary: Dana tells Marcus everything and asks him to be on the same side for once; he shows up. The school moves the fifth graders off the bus and adds a monitor. Tasha's draft is deleted. Dana thanks Renée — and sets a boundary. The four of them start a pickup group chat, and Lily names it.
